ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-intensity (white) pixels dominate approximately 85% of the visible ventral surface, while low-intensity (black) pixels occupy approximately 15%, concentrated along the trailing edge and the central peduncle junction.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Contiguous high-intensity white field across the interior of both lobes. A continuous low-intensity black band defines the trailing edge boundary. A large, irregular low-intensity black geometric blob is located at the center-base (peduncle junction). Sparse, isolated low-intensity circular spots are scattered across the white interior field.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Sharp V-shaped central depression with a calculated interior angle of approximately 45 degrees; vertical depth occupies roughly 12% of the total visible fluke height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serrations across the entire trailing edge boundary. Pixel-amplitude variations range from minor peaks (3-5 pixels) to significant valleys (15-20 pixels), notably on the left-inner and right-outer segments.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Trailing edges exhibit a slight convex curve leading to the distal tips. Leading edges (ventral-facing) show a consistent convex taper converging at the peduncle.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Multiple localized low-intensity circular pixel clusters (mottling) detected: five distinct clusters on the left lobe and four on the right lobe, primarily in the mid-to-inner regions.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Visible deep indentation/notch on the left lobe trailing edge boundary approximately one-third lateral from the median notch; irregular, ragged pixel boundaries at both distal lobe tips suggest cumulative physical trauma or wear.
other_distinctive_markers: Unique hourglass-shaped black pigmentation pattern at the fluke-peduncle junction, bisecting the lower white field.
